newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong sees Domco buy raising oper net.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong sees Domco buy raising oper net.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc's proposed acquisition of Domco Inc would be accretive to earnings, before one-time charges, Armstrong Chairman and Chief Executive George Lorch said Monday.

Lorch, detailing Armstrong's surprise C$23-per-share bid for the Canadian company, also said in a conference call that the transaction was not contingent on financing and would not prevent Armstrong from making future strategic investments.
He said he does not envision any manufacturing redundancies if the flooring companies combine.
Less than 48 hours after rejecting Armstrong's bid, Sommer accepted a US$562 million offer from Tarkett A.G., a German flooring manufacturer, for its flooring assets and its stake in Domco.

In a letter to Sommer, dated today, announcing Armstrong's bid for Domco, Lorch called the Tarkett deal "a complicated, highly leveraged business combination" that was worth "substantially less than the amount proposed by Armstrong on a comparable basis."

In today's conference call, Lorch said, "Under the Sommer-Tarkett transaction, there is no value for Domco minority shareholers. At a minimum, nothing changes for them. There is no premium, no buyout consideration and no hope of anything to come."
He said Armstrong would prefer to reach a negotiated agreement to acquire Domco.
Domco shares rallied on the Toronto Stock Exchange on the Armstrong bid, rising 6.75 to 21.50, easing off an earlier high of 22.50.
Armstrong shares were unchanged at 68-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
